value.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
value.text: Bobby leads the break-in at the old mansion to free Rogue from Cerebro, then stays behind to hold off the Sentinels so she can escape.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Her ex. Holds off the Sentinels so she can escape.
value.on_b_card_about_a: His ex. He frees her from Cerebro.

verdicts.why: The Rogue Cut rescue is right, and friend fits since Bobby is with Kitty now. But Bobby dies at the temple in the theatrical cut, so the killing (and 'dies' on both cards) is cut to what both cuts allow.

value.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
value.text: With Xavier guiding them, Magneto and Bobby break into the old mansion and free Rogue from Cerebro. When Bobby stays behind to hold off the Sentinels, Magneto gets her back to the X-Jet.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Once his captive. Freed by him from Cerebro.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Once her kidnapper. Frees her from her prison in Cerebro.

verdicts.why: The rescue and the turn to ally are right. 'After Bobby falls' clashes with the theatrical cut, where he dies later at the temple, so it is reworded.

Rogue Cut: Xavier agrees to rescue Rogue, guides Magneto and Bobby telepathically, shakes a Sentinel off the X-Jet and gets her away; Rogue then takes Kitty's place holding Logan's mind. Nothing in it clashes with the theatrical cut.
Rogue Cut: Rogue copies Kitty's power and keeps Logan's mind in 1973, and Wolverine appears to feel her presence in the past.

verdicts.why: A real exchange, and the new tie is right. 'Bobby didn't make it' is false for the theatrical cut, where Bobby is still alive at the temple then, so it is dropped.

value.text: When Kitty is hurt, Bobby tells Xavier that Rogue is held in Cerebro and could take her place. Xavier agrees to the rescue and guides Bobby into the old mansion.

verdicts.why: The text is right for the Rogue Cut. Xavier's card line 'dies on the rescue' is false for the theatrical cut, where Bobby dies at the temple, so it is reworded. Earlier stages: see item 23.
Rogue Cut: Iceman and Magneto break into the mansion and free Rogue, and Iceman holds off the Sentinels so the others can escape. It names no place of death, so it holds for both cuts.

verdicts.why: Kitty phasing Magneto inside is Rogue Cut only. In the theatrical cut Blink's portal brings him in, so a theatrical viewer would find the proposed text false. Both cuts share Magneto holding Logan down after Logan wounds Kitty.

Rogue Cut argument: Bishop says 'Some of us may never be born' and asks for a vote, and Xavier answers 'They just did. They're in.' Theatrical has only silent reaction shots there, so nothing clashes.
Rogue Cut: Blink argues 'We could keep going. Keep fighting', and Xavier and Storm answer the group until Bishop's people agree.
Rogue Cut: Sunspot objects that they are asked to die for a future they may not be part of, and Magneto and Xavier answer him.
Rogue Cut: Storm's speech answers Bishop's objection head on ('keep sending Bishop back in time... until one day he doesn't make it').
Rogue Cut: Storm answers Blink's 'We could keep going' directly with 'Until what?'.
Rogue Cut: Sunspot's objection answers Storm's speech, and the group, Sunspot included, goes along with the plan.
More Fun Stuff Version: Betty interviews Ned, her ex, and asks him about questionable late-night texts. Kind friend matches the tie.
More Fun Stuff Version: Betty interviews Flash, who claims he gave Spider-Man his name. A real exchange between classmates, so the new tie stands. Friend fits like Betty and Liz.

Both cuts: Wade shoots the Weapon XI Wade in front of Logan ('Hey! It's me! Don't scratch! Just cleaning up the timelines!'). Only the Super Duper Cut adds 'one day your old pal Wade's gonna ask you to get back in the saddle... say yes', and that line only adds, it contradicts nothing. Needs Deadpool 2 in Logan's titles (item 27).

value.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
value.text: Bobby fights the Sentinels in Moscow to buy Kitty time. At the temple they kiss before she sends Logan back, and later he dies holding off the Sentinels while she keeps Logan's mind in the past.
value.on_a_card_about_b: His girlfriend. Keeps Logan's mind in the past.

value.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
value.text: Bobby is among the last X-Men who hold off the Sentinels while Logan's mind is in the past, and he is killed.
value.on_a_card_about_b: One of the last X-Men holding off the Sentinels.
value.on_b_card_about_a: The X-Man whose trip to 1973 Bobby fights to protect.

verdicts.why: Reword both. In the Rogue Cut Bobby dies at the mansion, but Kitty is still holding Logan's mind then, so 'dies holding off the Sentinels while she keeps Logan's mind in the past' is true for both cuts. The Logan stage just drops 'at the temple'. The card lines also say 'temple' (live file: 'Fights to buy Kitty time in Moscow and at the temple.', 'One of the last X-Men defending the temple.'), so they change too. In the live Kitty stage, whoA describes Bobby though a is Bobby. Check that a/b order when applying. Kind partner per item 20.

value.text: Bobby fights the Sentinels in Moscow to buy Kitty time. At the temple they kiss before she sends Logan back, and later he dies holding off the Sentinels while she keeps Logan's mind in the past.
value.on_a_card_about_b: His girlfriend. Keeps Logan's mind in the past.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Her boyfriend. Dies fighting the Sentinels.

verdicts.why: The Rogue Cut is part of the film, and there Kitty is dating Bobby (Wikipedia), with a kiss and 'I'll see you in the next life'. The theatrical cut doesn't contradict it, so friend is now wrong and partner is right. Same stage as item 19.

The Paris stage is true for both cuts and still the main turn between them in the film. The Rogue Cut night is a near-rekindling ('nearly rekindles'), not a turn, so the evidence rule leaves the stage as it is.

value.text: As Logan prepares to go back to 1973, Bishop warns him that changing history could mean some of them are never born.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Warns him that changing history could erase them.
value.on_b_card_about_a: The X-Man sent back to change history.

value.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
value.text: When Sunspot asks if they are being told to give up their lives for a future they may not be part of, Magneto answers yes.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Balks at giving his life for the plan.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Tells him the plan is worth his life.

verdicts.why: The transcript shows two direct exchanges: Bishop answers Logan ('It's a risk... Not just for you. You do this, you change history'), and Magneto answers Sunspot's question with 'Yes'. Magneto with Bishop or Blink, and Logan with Blink or Sunspot, have no direct exchange there. Blink's portal for Magneto is theatrical only (Kitty does it in the Rogue Cut), so those stay out.

value.title: X-Men: The Last Stand
value.text: At Alcatraz, Bobby's ice wall stops Magneto's charging Brotherhood, and Magneto lets Pyro go down to finish him.
value.on_a_card_about_b: An X-Man who stops his Brotherhood at Alcatraz.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Sends Pyro after him at Alcatraz.

verdicts.why: Yes for two of them. X2: Xavier stops the museum fight Bobby is in, and Bobby and Rogue bring the jet in to save everyone. Last Stand: Magneto sends Pyro against Bobby. X-Men (2000) and other titles have no sourced exchange. Iceman and the Sentinels share only DOFP, so no earlier stage (item 7 covers both cuts). Medium confidence: from the fandom biography.

value.title: Daredevil (2003)
value.text: Foggy calls Ben at the morgue with the name of the man behind his informant's murder, the Kingpin's aide Wesley.
value.on_a_card_about_b: A reporter he tips off about Wesley.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Matt's partner. Tells him who killed his informant.

verdicts.why: The Director's Cut has a verbal exchange between Foggy and Wesley at the Natchios party ('What a dick!'). Foggy then solves the WOW clue and phones Urich, which leads Manolis to offer Wesley a plea deal. No source has Foggy facing Fisk. Adding Daunte Jackson, McKenzie and Karen Page (Karen is in the theatrical cut too) is a roster question the rules don't cover, so it is left to the owner.

value.title: The Punisher (2004)
value.text: Jimmy is Frank's partner and old friend, who sees him off to the family reunion. He has sold Frank out to Howard Saint, and when Frank finds out he leaves Jimmy a single bullet to kill himself.
value.on_a_card_about_b: His partner and old friend. Sells him out to Saint.
value.on_b_card_about_a: His partner and old friend. Makes him pay for the betrayal.

value.title: The Punisher (2004)
value.text: Howard learns of Jimmy's gambling debts and corners him at a casino, forcing him to name the agent behind Bobby's death.
value.on_a_card_about_b: An indebted agent he forces to give up Frank.
value.on_b_card_about_a: A crime boss who uses his debts to turn him.

verdicts.why: Add the person first: Jimmy Weeks is in the theatrical cast too ('Frank's partner in the FBI'; the farewell at the party and the press-conference stairs scene are in both cuts), and the extended cut builds the betrayal around him. That puts him well above the bar of people already listed (Mickey Duka, the Toro brothers). New person, e.g. pr-jimmy-weeks 'Jimmy Weeks', 'Frank's FBI partner and old army friend', titles ['The Punisher (2004)'], then these two stages.

value.title: Spider-Man 2
value.text: Peter meets Rosie when he visits Otto, and she joins their talk about his fusion work. She is killed at the demonstration Peter attends.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Otto's wife. Killed at his demonstration.
value.on_b_card_about_a: A young student who visits Otto.

verdicts.why: Both cuts: May fetches the villains in her F.E.A.S.T. truck and takes them into Happy's apartment to be cured. She asks Otto 'Fresh water or salt?', Connors tells her he will stay in the truck, and then Electro cuts the power and stops the elevators as she runs down. The More Fun Stuff Version only adds the elevator ride. May with Connors is also untied, so it is added (medium). Spider-Man 2: Peter's long meeting with Otto and Rosie ('He's done his homework', fandom), and Rosie dies at the demonstration Peter attends.

Add 'Deadpool 2' to fox-wolverine's titles. He is on screen in both cuts in the post-credits scene (reused X-Men Origins: Wolverine footage, 'much to the surprise of Wolverine'), so the item 18 stage can show. Keep that stage.
